applied.summary: AC4 carried NET-NEW fail-closed-allowlist material (missing/unreadable/mode-wider-than-0600 ⇒ refuse all) under the P1.10 INV-POLICY-4 surviving-clause banner, which R2 §5 shows covers only the unauthorized-approver case. Split the attribution: INV-POLICY-4 cited for the unauthorized-approver half, fail-closed explicitly marked NET-NEW per DD-8 so it gets fresh review rather than 'survives verbatim, do not re-litigate'.

attach was an unbounded, unauthenticated privilege surface: DF3.6 Trigger Surface routes 'operator raising a bound mid-run via attach' to DF3.4 as follow-up, but DF3.4 neither claimed nor forbade it, and INV-APPROVE-5 forbade only gate approve/reject/skip/reorder — silent on spend ceilings and steering-iteration bounds. Rewrote INV-APPROVE-5 as 'steering carries no privilege': attach is guidance text only (matching DF3.3's directive rule), never raises a ceiling or bound, DF3.6's bounds immutable mid-run, so attach grants no privilege and needs none beyond host-local CLI access. Closes DF3.6's dangling pointer from this side.

Sweep-vs-decision ordering was unspecified with lazy expiry and no daemon, leaving a human approve landing after expiresAt able to reach 'approved'. Guards/limits now states expiry is evaluated before that invocation's own decision, so a late decision finds 'timed-out' and is refused.

Approver allowlist had a rotation mechanism but no revocation-propagation statement (secrets-invariants least-privilege/rotation). Now states the allowlist is re-read per decision so a rotated or removed entry takes effect immediately; kept stdin-never-argv, constant-time, never-logged within the same 3 lines.
Infra Prerequisites allowlist row cross-referenced '(AC5)' for the absent/loose-⇒-refuse behavior; that is AC4 (AC5 is attach). Corrected.

DoD Security bullet did not name the unknown-approver negative case (auth-invariants 'negative-auth test per endpoint'). Reworded to require an unknown approver and a missing/0644 allowlist each refuse with no state change.

AC2's forbidden hand-rolled-command list omitted 'git push', which INV-SKILL-3 and the DoD both carry — leaving the D8/DD-10 push-credential boundary unenforced by any AC. Added 'git push' to AC2 with the D8 citation.

AC6 cited DF3.4 INV-APPROVE-2 for the token-on-stdin fact; stdin delivery is INV-APPROVE-6 (INV-APPROVE-2 is the allowlist authorization). Now cites INV-APPROVE-6 for stdin and INV-APPROVE-2 for authorization staying in the gate, matching INV-SKILL-1's already-correct pointer.

Files to Modify listed src/fleet/verbs.ts and scripts/fleet.ts, contradicting the story's own DoD ('no second list is introduced') and inviting the double-implementation R5 §5.4 guards against. Moved both to an explicit read-only note: consumed unmodified from DF3.1, this story adds a second consumer of listVerbs(), never a second source.

Bare 'SKILL.md:19-22' / ':33-36' / ':13-25' refs were ambiguous between the two distinct INK files cited in Spec Reference (sssf-sandbox-orchestrator and sssf). Prefixed all four with 'orchestrator'. Verified against the live reference repo: :13-25 is THIN SKILL FAT RECIPES, :19-22 is the never-hand-roll-a-mint/revoke/ssh rule, :33-36 is the one-command preflight with report-and-stop — all three citations are substantively exact.

surviving.summary: DoD Security bullet uses the shorthand '(INV-APPROVE-2/3)' rather than naming both invariants in full; unambiguous in context, left as-is because the story sits at 199/200 normative lines.

tests/fleet/fixtures/approvers.json is not stated to use obviously-fake sentinel token values (secrets-invariants 'fixture secrets are obviously fake'). Low real risk — the fixture stores salted hashes of test tokens by construction — and no line budget remained to state it.
